provenance.note: Curated flagship register across the 9 MMR corporations - per-record `sources` citations carry the accountability. confidence grades V/N/C per the legacy note (C = sources conflict, both figures shown); areas in acres as reported, some estimates; Marathi names are transliterations unless a Marathi source confirmed them.

note: Curated flagship water bodies across the Mumbai Metropolitan Region's 9 corporations, compiled 2026-06 from sourced reporting. confidence: V = verified across sources, N = single/secondary source (needs verification), C = sources conflict (both figures shown). Areas given in acres where reported; some are estimates. Names in Marathi are transliterations unless a Marathi source confirmed them.

bodies.name: Powai Lake
bodies.status: Drinking source long abandoned; eutrophic with ~18 MLD untreated sewage inflow (BMC affidavit cites ~10.9 MLD); hyacinth cover reported at 23-25% (BMC ops, Apr 2024) vs 80% (NGT/press framing, Jul 2025); ~Rs 66 cr restoration with an 8 MLD STP not commissioned until Dec 2027.
bodies.cultural_note: Beside IIT Bombay; still hosts 18+ wild mugger crocodiles (2022 BMC census). Mumbai's clearest emblem of a water source lost to sewage.
bodies.location_basis: OSM lake polygon centroid beside IIT Bombay

bodies.name: Vihar Lake
bodies.status: Active supply (~3% of Mumbai); inside Sanjay Gandhi National Park; max depth ~34 m; mugger crocodiles.
bodies.cultural_note: Largest lake within Mumbai city limits and the headwater impoundment of the Mithi - the river behind the 26 July 2005 flood.
bodies.location_basis: OSM reservoir polygon centroid inside SGNP

bodies.name: Tulsi Lake
bodies.status: Smallest of Mumbai's drinking reservoirs; forest-buffered inside SGNP, commonly cited as the cleanest (qualitative); mugger crocodiles.
bodies.cultural_note: The encroachment-free counterpoint to Powai - same city, opposite fate.
bodies.location_basis: OSM reservoir polygon centroid, SGNP north of Vihar

bodies.name: Bandra Talao
bodies.status: Grade-II heritage tank; dewatered May 2026 for a ~Rs 20 cr BMC restoration (15th Finance Commission); activist criticism of the cost/approach.
bodies.cultural_note: Test case for reviving Mumbai's small heritage talaos as blue-green assets.
bodies.location_basis: OSM water polygon at S.V. Road near Bandra (W) station

bodies.name: Banganga Talao
bodies.feed: Spring-fed (freshwater within metres of the sea)
bodies.status: Sacred heritage tank at Malabar Hill; a Sept 2025 Bombay HC order refused idol immersion here ('right to clean water prevails').
bodies.cultural_note: A 'right to clean water' immersion precedent for heritage tanks statewide.
bodies.location_basis: OSM Banganga Tank polygon, Walkeshwar, Malabar Hill

bodies.name: Masunda Lake
bodies.era: Cited ~1,200 years old (journalistic, not archaeologically confirmed)
bodies.status: Iconic and actively used (400 m glass pathway, 2020), but greenish water, foul odour and blocked inlets reported; reduced ~1/3 by a 1950s station road.
bodies.cultural_note: The emotional and civic centre of 'City of Lakes' Thane, with an island Shiva temple and 1964 Shivaji statue; Navratri immersion.
bodies.location_basis: OSM 'Talao Pali' lake polygon beside Thane station

bodies.name: Upvan Lake
bodies.builder: J.K. Singhania (reconstructed to supply the Raymond textile factory)
bodies.status: Flagship recreational lake (Sanskruti arts festival, ~50,000+ visitors); cited as a hardscape-'beautification' example. Area conflicting: ~6 ha (Wikipedia) vs ~26 acres (travel sources).
bodies.cultural_note: Thane's flagship public-realm lake at the foot of Yeoor Hills.
bodies.location_basis: OSM lake polygon at Shivai Nagar, foot of Yeoor Hills

bodies.name: Kacharali Lake
bodies.status: Beautified and well-maintained, opposite the TMC headquarters; on the AMRUT-2 conservation list.
bodies.cultural_note: Thane's showcase lake beside the municipal HQ - the maintained-flagship reference.
bodies.location_basis: OSM lake polygon at Panch Pakhadi, opposite TMC HQ

bodies.name: Siddheshwar Talao
bodies.era: King Bimba era (a 9th-c Brahma idol was found during cleaning)
bodies.status: Severely degraded - slum sewage on three sides, hyacinth, fish kills, shrinking to encroachment - and pointedly excluded from the City-of-Lakes conservation campaign.
bodies.cultural_note: The counter-narrative: a priceless temple tank left to rot because it isn't a marketable public-realm site.

bodies.name: Makhmali Talao
bodies.status: Degraded and neglected - poor water quality, a non-functional aerator, food-dumping - and left out of the AMRUT-2 funding list; subject of the citizen 'Majha Talao' awareness campaign.
bodies.cultural_note: The neighbourhood-tank gap behind Thane's flagship beautified lakes.
bodies.location_basis: OSM Makhamali Talaav polygon, Thane east

bodies.name: Kavesar Lake
bodies.status: Thane's last natural wetland (200+ species; the district's only naturally-growing white lotus); a ~Rs 6-7 cr TMC beautification is opposed by the Save Kavesar Lake movement (8,000+ signatures) who argue it would destroy the ecology.
bodies.cultural_note: The clearest 'governance not water' case: citizens fighting beautification to save an ecological lake.

bodies.name: Thane Creek Flamingo Sanctuary
bodies.status: Ramsar Site No. 2490 (designated 27 Dec 2022, first in MMR); Wildlife Sanctuary 1,690.5 ha core + 4,832 ha ESZ; BNHS counted >130,000 flamingos in 2022.
bodies.cultural_note: The anchor wetland ecosystem; the Navi Mumbai satellite wetlands below are hydrologically linked feeders.

bodies.name: DPS Flamingo Lake
bodies.status: Declared a Conservation Reserve (17 Apr 2025) - then targeted by a CIDCO de-reservation resolution days later; flamingo deaths in 2024 after a water-flow disruption, return in 2025 after partial tidal restoration.
bodies.cultural_note: The flagship citizen-vs-CIDCO wetland fight in Navi Mumbai.
bodies.location_basis: OSM DPS Lake tidal polygon behind DPS Nerul

bodies.name: NRI Wetland
bodies.status: The original 'golf course vs flamingos' battle (37 waterbird species); Bombay HC struck down the golf course (2018, total ban on NWIA-wetland reclamation); the developer's SLP is still pending in the Supreme Court; a recommended Conservation Reserve status is undeclared.
bodies.cultural_note: An unresolved Supreme Court matter on Palm Beach Road, Seawoods.
bodies.location_basis: OSM NRI Lake polygon, Seawoods, Palm Beach Road

bodies.name: Kala Talao
bodies.status: 'Beautified' with a track, boating and fountain yet still acidic (pH 3.9-4.25), sewage-fed and eutrophic; Ganesh immersion.
bodies.cultural_note: Kalyan's beautified-but-still-acidic paradox - the cosmetic-vs-real-restoration gap in the outer MMR.

bodies.name: Vadale Lake
bodies.status: Rs 13 cr beautification (2021); Phase-2 boating cancelled on ecological grounds (Sep 2024); now nature-based weed control (>1 lakh Salvinia weevils with ICAR-DWR Jabalpur, 2026-27); ~32 bird species. Open-water area conflicting (25/22/~9 acres after encroachment).
bodies.cultural_note: Old Panvel's temple lake by the Ballaleshwar shrine - the outer MMR's cleanest nature-based restoration arc.
bodies.location_basis: OSM Ballaleshwar Lake polygon, Old Panvel
